newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Giscard - BoF need not follow Buba rate.
newsitem.headline: France's Giscard - BoF need not follow Buba rate.

text.p: Former French President Valery Giscard D'Estaing on Thursday said that if Germany's Bundesbank raised interest rates, the Bank of France would have no reason to follow suit.
"If it were the case that the Bundesbank decided to raise its rates, there would be no reason for the Bank of France to increase its rates," he said in an article in the weekly magazine L'Express.
He added that he did not believe the German central bank would tighten monetary policy.
"Even if the Bundesbank did raise short-term rates slightly, that would bring them close to our rates, which would correspond pretty closely to the situation in our two countries," he wrote.
The Bank of France's key intervention rate stands at 3.10 percent while the German repo rate is at 3.0 percent.

Speculation about a possible German rate rise was revived this week when the Bundesbank said in its monthly report that German inflation had picked up and that it would steer policy to ensure price stability was maintained.
That boosted the mark, pushing it to its highest level in two weeks against the dollar.
